headings: Our Approach to Development of Precision Medicines in Oncology
paragraphs: We are a biopharmaceutical company committed to realizing the promise of precision medicines for the treatment of cancer. Since our founding in 2014, we have transformed from a research and development company to a fully-integrated commercial-stage organization with a diversified pipeline of product candidates. Our pipeline consists of small molecules designed to target cancer signaling pathways and address significant unmet needs in oncology and hematology.

2025 was a pivotal year for our company. On November 13, 2025, the FDA approved our new drug application, or NDA, for ziftomenib, which is being marketed in the United States under the trade name KOMZIFTITM, for the treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia, or AML, with a susceptible nucleophosmin 1, or NPM1, mutation who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options. KOMZIFTI is the first and only menin inhibitor approved by the FDA for once-daily oral administration.

We continue to evaluate ziftomenib across the AML treatment continuum, including in relapsed or refractory and newly diagnosed disease and in patient subtypes representing up to 50% of AML cases. Among other studies, our clinical development program includes two registrational Phase 3 clinical trials of ziftomenib in combination with intensive and non-intensive chemotherapy in patients with newly diagnosed AML and multiple clinical trials of ziftomenib in combination with standards of care in patients with relapsed or refractory and newly diagnosed AML with NPM1 and FLT3 co-mutations.
In addition to AML, we are evaluating ziftomenib in combination with imatinib for the treatment of gastrointestinal stromal tumors, or GIST.

We also are exploring the use of KO-7246, a next-generation menin inhibitor, for use in diabetes and cardiometabolic disorders and additional next-generation menin inhibitors for use in combination with other therapies in solid tumors.

In addition to our menin inhibitor programs, we are evaluating farnesyl transferase inhibitors, or FTIs, in combination with various targeted therapies to address mechanisms of adaptive and innate resistance in the treatment of solid tumors. Our lead FTI product candidate is darlifarnib, which we are evaluating in combination with certain targeted therapies in large solid tumor indications, including renal cell carcinoma, or RCC, non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC, colorectal cancer, or CRC, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, or PDAC. We also are evaluating opportunities to partner darlifarnib with novel PI3 Kinase alpha, or PI3K alpha, and RAS inhibitors in additional indications.

We plan to advance our product candidates through a combination of internal development, strategic partnerships and clinical collaborations while maintaining significant development and commercial rights.

Progress bars in the pipeline above indicate the stage of development based on ongoing or completed activities. A partial bar indicates a phase in progress; a full bar indicates completion of a phase. Bars do not represent scale, duration, or likelihood of success.

Our strategy is to discover, acquire, develop and commercialize innovative agents in oncology indications and other diseases with significant unmet medical need and attractive commercial potential. The key components of our strategy include the following:
• Establish KOMZIFTI as the leading menin inhibitor in relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML, with the goal of achieving majority class share;
• Generate data to advance ziftomenib into earlier lines of treatment and establish it as a foundational combination partner with standard-of-care therapies;

• Develop novel, targeted small molecule product candidates for the treatment of cancer and other diseases, including in combination with existing therapies, such as established standards of care, to deepen clinical responses and extend the durability of benefit, while maintaining manageable safety profiles;

• Identify molecular, genetic or tumor-related characteristics of patients most likely to benefit from our product candidates, leveraging clinical and pathology trends towards comprehensive molecular and genomic profiling and companion diagnostics; and

• Build a sustainable product pipeline and advance our programs through a combination of internal discovery and development and accessing external innovation through strategic partnerships, collaborations, in-licenses and acquisitions, while maintaining significant development and commercial rights to our product candidates.

headings: Risks Related to the Commercialization of KOMZIFTI and Our Product Candidates
KOMZIFTI may fail to achieve the degree of market acceptance by physicians, patients, third-party payors and others in the medical community necessary for commercial success.
If the market opportunities for KOMZIFTI are smaller than we believe, our revenue may be adversely affected, and our business may suffer.
If we are unable to execute on our sales, marketing and distribution plans to commercialize KOMZIFTI, we may be unable to generate meaningful product revenue.
Post-approval results for KOMZIFTI in larger numbers of patients, broader populations or real world clinical practice may not be consistent with the results from our clinical trials.
We have limited experience as a commercial company and our sales, marketing and distribution of KOMZIFTI may be unsuccessful or less successful than anticipated.
Product liability lawsuits against us could cause us to incur substantial liabilities and to limit commercialization of KOMZIFTI or any other approved products.
Risks Related to Regulatory Approval of Our Product and Product Candidates and Other Legal Compliance Matters
We may be unable to maintain FDA approval of KOMZIFTI for adult patients with relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML, which would severely and adversely affect our business and business prospects.
Failure to obtain marketing approval in international jurisdictions would prevent our product candidates from being marketed abroad.

KOMZIFTI is our only approved product and it has been approved solely as a monotherapy for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML. Prior to KOMZIFTI, we have not, as an organization, launched or commercialized a product, and there is no guarantee that we will be able to do so successfully with KOMZIFTI. Our ability to generate revenue and achieve profitability is wholly dependent on our ability to successfully commercialize KOMZIFTI in the United States and to expand ziftomenib's indications for use beyond monotherapy in adult patients with relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML.

References to "Kura Oncology, Inc.," "we," "us" and "our" refer to Kura Oncology, Inc. Overview

We are a biopharmaceutical company committed to realizing the promise of precision medicines for the treatment of cancer. Since our founding in 2014, we have transformed from a research and development company to a fully-integrated commercial-stage organization with a diversified pipeline of product candidates. Our pipeline consists of small molecules designed to target cancer signaling pathways and address significant unmet needs in oncology and hematology.

On November 13, 2025, the FDA approved our NDA for ziftomenib, which is being marketed in the United States under the trade name KOMZIFTI, for the treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory AML with a susceptible NPM1 mutation who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options. KOMZIFTI is the first and only menin inhibitor approved by the FDA for once-daily oral administration. The FDA previously granted Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designations as well as Priority Review to ziftomenib.

FDA approval of our NDA for KOMZIFTI was based upon positive data from our KOMET-001 trial, a global Phase 1/2 trial that evaluated KOMZIFTI's safety and efficacy in 112 patients with relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML.

We believe that KOMZIFTI is differentiated from other menin inhibitors on the four pillars of efficacy, safety, compatibility and simplicity, and our market research indicates that this differentiated profile aligns with the priorities of physicians, pharmacists and care teams who treat patients with AML as well as with third-party payors, including commercial insurers and government healthcare programs.

Efficacy: The rate of CR+CRh in the KOMET-001 trial was 21.4% (95% CI: 14.2, 30.2). The median duration of CR+CRh was five months (95% CI: 1.9, 8.1) and the median time to first response in patients who achieved a CR or CRh was 2.7 months (range: 0.9 to 15 months). 88% of patients who achieved CR or CRh did so within six months of initiating KOMZIFTI. These data from the Prescribing Information for KOMZIFTI are generally consistent with the full results of the KOMET-001 trial published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in September 2025.

Safety: KOMZIFTI demonstrated a manageable safety profile in the KOMET-001 trial, with most reported adverse events being Grade 1 or Grade 2. The most common adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, reported in 20% or more of patients were aspartate aminotransferase increased, infection without an identified pathogen, potassium decreased, albumin decreased, alanine aminotransferase increased, sodium decreased, creatinine increased, alkaline phosphatase increased, hemorrhage, diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, edema, bacterial infection, musculoskeletal pain, bilirubin increased, potassium increased, DS, pruritus, febrile neutropenia and transaminases increased. Notably, no Grade 4 or Grade 5 QTc interval prolongation was reported. 12% of patients experienced QTc interval prolongation of ≤ Grade 3 and, of the 70 patients 65 years of age or older, 10% experienced QTc interval prolongation of any cause.

The Prescribing Information for KOMZIFTI includes a Black Box warning for DS, a well-studied mechanism-based risk in drugs that restore differentiation, and clear dose-modification guidelines for physicians to follow when DS is
suspected. Unlike the other FDA-approved menin inhibitor, KOMZIFTI does not have Black Box warning for QTc interval prolongations or Torsades de Pointes.

Compatibility: In contrast with other therapies that require dose adjustments when co-administered with anti-infective medications or other strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, KOMZIFTI can be co-administered without dose modification, offering predictability to physicians and reducing complexity and risk.

Simplicity: KOMZIFTI is the first and only menin inhibitor approved by the FDA for once-daily oral administration. KOMZIFTI's once-daily dosing is beneficial to patients who are often elderly and on several concomitant medications.

We initiated commercial sales of KOMZIFTI in the United States on November 21, 2025. Under the terms of the Kyowa License Agreement, we lead commercial strategy for and are responsible for manufacturing KOMZIFTI in the United States. We and Kyowa Kirin are jointly performing commercialization and medical affairs activities in accordance with a co-created U.S. territory commercialization plan and the Kyowa Co-Promotion Agreement. We record all U.S. sales of KOMZIFTI, and we and Kyowa Kirin share equally the profits and losses from the commercialization activities in the United States. Outside the United States, Kyowa Kirin is responsible for commercial strategy and for commercializing ziftomenib and booking sales.
On November 25, 2025, we announced that KOMZIFTI was added to the NCCN Guidelines® as a Category 2A recommended treatment option for adults with relapsed or refractory NPM1-mutated AML.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家生技藥品公司，致力於實現精準醫療在癌症治療上的潛力。自2014年成立以來，我們已從一家研究與開發公司轉型為一家完整整合的商業階段組織，擁有多元化的產品候選藥物組合。我們的產品組合包含小分子藥物，設計用以針對癌症訊號傳導路徑，並解決血液學與腫瘤學領域的重大未滿足醫療需求。
2025年對本公司而言是關鍵的一年。2025年11月13日，美國食品藥物管理局核准我們的新藥申請，或NDA，針對ziftomenib，該藥物在美國以商品名KOMZIFTI銷售，用以治療無滿意替代治療選擇的成人急性髓細胞白血病，或AML，具有易感性核仁磷酸化蛋白1，或NPM1，突變的患者。KOMZIFTI為美國食品藥物管理局核准的首個且唯一可每日一次口服的menin抑制劑。
我們持續評估ziftomenib在AML治療連續體中的應用，包括在復發或難治性及新診斷的疾病，以及代表最多50%AML病例的患者亞型。在其他研究中，我們的臨牀開發計畫包含兩項註冊性第三期臨牀試驗，評估ziftomenib與強度及非強度化療合併使用於新診斷AML患者，以及多項臨牀試驗評估ziftomenib與標準療法合併使用於復發或難治性及新診斷AML患者，且具有NPM1與FLT3共突變的患者。
除了AML之外，我們也在評估ziftomenib與imatinib合併使用，用以治療胃腸道神經內分泌腫瘤，或GIST。
我們也正在探索KO-7246，一種新一代menin抑制劑，用於糖尿病與心臟代謝疾病，以及其他新一代menin抑制劑用於與其他療法合併使用於實體腫瘤的應用。

除了我們的menin抑制劑計畫，我們也在評估法呢斯轉移酶抑制劑，或FTIs，與各種標靶療法合併使用，以解決實體腫瘤治療中的適應性與先天性抗藥機制。我們的領先FTI產品候選藥物為darlifarnib，我們正在評估其與某些標靶療法合併使用於大型實體腫瘤適應症，包括腎細胞癌，或RCC，非小細胞肺癌，或NSCLC，結腸直腸癌，或CRC，以及胰臟導管腺癌，或PDAC。我們也正在評估將darlifarnib與新型PI3 Kinase alpha，或PI3K alpha，及RAS抑制劑合併使用於其他適應症的機會。
我們計畫透過內部開發、戰略合作與臨牀合作，推進我們的產品候選藥物，同時維持重要的開發與商業權利。
上述產品組閤中的進度條顯示根據持續或已完成的活動所處的開發階段。部分條表示階段進行中；完整條表示階段已完成。條不代表規模、持續時間或成功機率。
本公司策略為發現、取得、開發及商業化具創新性之藥物，用於腫瘤學領域及其他具有重大未滿足醫療需求且具備吸引人商業潛力之疾病。本公司策略之關鍵零組件如下：
• 建立 KOMZIFTI 為治療復發或難治性 NPM1 突變 AML 之主要 menin 抑制劑，目標為取得主要市場佔有率；
• 產生數據以推動 ziftomenib 進入較早治療線路，並建立其為標準療法之基礎組合夥伴；
• 開發新型、具針對性之小分子產品候選藥物，用於治療癌症及其他疾病，包括與現有療法（如已建立之標準療法）組合使用，以深化臨牀反應並延長療效持續時間，同時維持可管理之安全性；
• 識別最可能從本公司產品候選藥物受益之患者之分子、遺傳或腫瘤相關特徵，利用臨牀及病理趨勢朝向全面分子及基因組分析與伴診診斷；
• 建立可持續之產品開發管道，並透過內部發現及開發與取得外部創新之戰略合作夥伴、合作計畫、進口授權及收購等方式推進本公司計畫，同時維持對本公司產品候選藥物之重大開發及商業權利。

paragraphs: 以下有關 Kura Oncology, Inc. 財務狀況及營運成果的討論，應與本年度報告中所載的財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。本討論與分析中所包含的部分資訊，或於本年度報告其他處所載明的資訊，包括有關本公司業務計畫與策略的資訊，包含風險、假設與不確定性等向前看陳述。可能導致實際結果與向前看陳述中所描述或暗示的結果有重大差異的重要因素，包括但不限於本年度報告中「項目 1A. 風險因素」所列者。本年度報告中所有向前看陳述均基於我們在提交本年度報告時所掌握的資訊，除非法律要求，否則我們不負有更新公開資訊或修訂任何向前看陳述的義務。有關 2024 年度財務結果與 2023 年度財務結果的比較，請參閱本年度報告中「項目 7，管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析」，該報告為 2024 年度財務年度結算報告，於 2025 年 2 月 28 日提交至 SEC。
提及「Kura Oncology, Inc.」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們」均指 Kura Oncology, Inc. 總覽
我們是一家生物製藥公司，致力於實現精準醫療在癌症治療上的潛力。自 2014 年成立以來，我們已從一家研究與開發公司轉型為一家完整的商業階段組織，擁有多元化的產品候選品項。我們的產品候選品項包含小分子藥物，設計用以針對癌症訊號傳導路徑，並解決血液學與腫瘤學中的重大未滿足需求。

2025 年 11 月 13 日，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准我們的 NDA（新藥申請）用於 ziftomenib，該藥品在美國以商品名 KOMZIFTI 銷售，用於治療無滿意替代治療選擇的成人急性骨髓性白血病（AML）患者，其具有易感的 NPM1 突變。KOMZIFTI 是美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准的第一且唯一一種每日一次口服的 menin 抑制劑。美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）先前已授予 ziftomenib 突破性療法、快速通道與罕見疾病藥物指定，以及優先審查。
美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准我們的 KOMZIFTI NDA 是基於我們 KOMET-001 試驗的正面數據，該試驗為一全球性的 Phase 1/2 試驗，評估 KOMZIFTI 在 112 名患有復發或難治性 NPM1 突變 AML 患者中的安全性與有效性。
我們認為 KOMZIFTI 與其他 menin 抑制劑相比，在有效性、安全性、相容性與簡易性四個支柱上有所區隔，且我們的市場研究顯示，這種區隔的特質與治療 AML 患者的醫師、藥師與照護團隊的優先事項，以及第三方付款者（包括商業保險公司與政府醫療計畫）的考量相符。

有效性：在 KOMET-001 試驗中，CR+CRh 的發生率為 21.4%（95% CI：14.2, 30.2）。CR+CRh 的中位持續時間為五個月（95% CI：1.9, 8.1），在達到 CR 或 CRh 的患者中，首次反應的中位時間為 2.7 個月（範圍：0.9 至 15 個月）。88% 的患者在開始使用 KOMZIFTI 後六個月內達到 CR 或 CRh。這些數據與 KOMZIFTI 的處方資訊一致，並與 2025 年 9 月發表於《臨牀腫瘤學雜誌》的 KOMET-001 試驗完整結果相符。

安全性：在 KOMET-001 試驗中，KOMZIFTI 顯示出可管理的安全性表現，大多數報告的不良事件為 Grade 1 或 Grade 2。在 20% 或更多患者中報告的最常見不良反應（包括實驗室異常）為天門冬氨酸氨基轉移酶升高、無已知病原體感染、血鉀降低、血清白蛋白降低、丙氨酸氨基轉移酶升高、血鈉降低、肌酐升高、鹼性磷酸酶升高、出血、腹瀉、噁心、疲勞、水腫、細菌感染、肌肉骨骼疼痛、膽紅素升高、血鉀升高、DS、癢、發熱性中性粒細胞減少症與轉氨酶升高。值得注意的是，未報告 Grade 4 或 Grade 5 的 QTc 間隔延長。12% 的患者出現 QTc 間隔延長為 ≤ Grade 3，而在 70 名 65 歲或以上年齡的患者中，10% 的患者出現任何原因的 QTc 間隔延長。
KOMZIFTI 的處方資訊包含針對 DS 的黑盒警告，DS 是一種在復原分化作用藥物中已廣為研究的機制性風險，並明確提供給醫師的劑量調整指引，用以在懷疑 DS 時遵循。
與其他 FDA 批准的 menin 抑製劑不同，KOMZIFTI 不具備針對 QTc 電壓延長或 Torsades de Pointes 的黑盒警告。
相容性：與其他在與抗感染藥物或其他強效或中度 CYP3A4 抑製劑或誘導劑同時使用時需要調整劑量的治療方式不同，KOMZIFTI 可以在不調整劑量的情況下同時使用，為醫師提供可預測性，並降低複雜性與風險。
簡化：KOMZIFTI 是美國 FDA 批准的首款且唯一可每日一次口服投與的 menin 抑製劑。KOMZIFTI 的每日一次投與方式對許多年長且同時服用多種藥物的患者而言是有利的。

我們於 2025 年 11 月 21 日開始在美國進行 KOMZIFTI 的商業銷售。根據 Kyowa 授權協議的條款，我們領導 KOMZIFTI 在美國的商業策略，並負責美國的製造工作。我們與 Kyowa Kirin 共同執行商業化與醫療事務活動，依照共同制定的美國地區商業化計畫與 Kyowa 共同推廣協議。我們記錄所有美國的 KOMZIFTI 銷售，我們與 Kyowa Kirin 共同分擔美國商業化活動的盈虧。
我們於 2025 年 11 月 25 日宣佈，KOMZIFTI 已被納入 NCCN 指南®，作為成年復發或難治性 NPM1 突變 AML 患者 Category 2A 推薦治療選項。

KOMZIFTI 是我們唯一核准之產品，且僅核准作為治療成人復發或難治性 NPM1-變異 AML 患者之單一療法。在 KOMZIFTI 之前，我們作為組織並未發行或商業化任何產品，且無法保證我們能成功以 KOMZIFTI 發行或商業化產品。我們產生收入與實現獲利之能力完全依賴我們能成功於美國商業化 KOMZIFTI，以及擴展 ziftomenib 之適應症使用，超越成人復發或難治性 NPM1-變異 AML 患者之單一療法。
